items.stem: Ransomware is actively spreading to a file share. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.text: Isolate affected systems from the network to contain the spread
options.rationale: Correct: containment limits damage while deeper response proceeds.
Paying is not an immediate technical containment and is discouraged.
Mass wiping destroys evidence and may be unnecessary.

options.text: Wait to see how far it spreads

items.explanation: Correct: isolating affected systems contains the spread first.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO steps protect evidence during an incident? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Capturing volatile data before powering a system off
options.rationale: Correct: volatile memory is lost on shutdown, so capture it first.

options.text: Recording who handled evidence and when
options.rationale: Correct: a chain of custody keeps evidence defensible.

options.text: Rebooting the system to clear the infection
Editing logs to remove confusing entries

items.explanation: Correct: capturing volatile data first and keeping a chain of custody both preserve evidence.

items.stem: Why run a post-incident review after recovery is complete?

options.text: To identify improvements that reduce the chance or impact of a repeat
options.rationale: Correct: lessons learned drive concrete preventive changes.

options.text: To assign personal blame to a staff member
options.rationale: Blame is not the purpose of a constructive review.

options.text: Because the incident is not really over otherwise
options.rationale: Recovery ends the incident; the review improves the future.

options.text: To delete all records of the incident
options.rationale: Records should be kept, not deleted.

items.explanation: Correct: the review turns the incident into concrete improvements.
